conclusion: Transfer application works when supplied. Missing semantic effects can pass validation, save conflicting prose/memory/canon, and affect later inventory scope.
limitations: Synthetic proposals demonstrate application gaps; they do not identify what the user’s actual model returned. Source anchoring checks quote presence, not semantic entailment. Item names need not be unique, so a duplicate-name check alone is not a safe fix. The recipient-scene probe excludes earlier mentions and memories to isolate ownership-based selection.
